subject: Data handling decision pathways for BrightPath - post-demo
messages:
From: Neha Kapoor <neha_kapoor@redwood.com>
To: Elaine Chu <elaine.chu@brightpath.ai>, Tim Lee <timothy.lee@brightpath.ai>
Cc: Aditya Rao <aditya_rao@redwood.com>, Monica Patel <monica_patel@redwood.com>
Date: Fri, 25 Sep 2026 15:12:00 -0700
Subject: Post-demo recap + data handling asks (BrightPath)

Hi Elaine / Tim — thanks again for taking the demo earlier. Quick recap of the open data/privacy items we captured and proposed next steps so we can move toward an SOW: 

1) Retention profile: BrightPath asked whether Redwood can support a 0-retention mode for inference logs that contain PII, plus a shortened retention window for service logs and KV traces.
2) Residency: you emphasized US-only residency for any persisted artifacts.
3) Evidence: you asked for SOC 2 artifacts and a short DPIA outline for internal review.

Proposed options (we discussed on the call):
- Option A: Hosted API with custom routing to a 0-retention processing path for PII (ephemeral only) — constrained for limited routes; requires a security exception and additional controls.
- Option B: Dedicated/Private deployment (VPC) where the customer controls logs; recommended when true zero-persist is mandatory.
- Option C: Hybrid: short retention (7 days) for debugging with role-based access and audit logs.

Next steps I propose: 
- Redwood to send a short technical note detailing what we mean by “0-retention” and the default telemetry we still collect (aggregated metrics, health signals).
- Security to propose contract language for a retention carveout and required audit evidence.
- Redwood to share DPIA skeleton and a draft SOW for BrightPath review (attached).

Can you confirm which option you want us to scope (A/B/C) and whether procurement should be looped now? If you prefer, we can open an internal security exception request and document proposed mitigations.

Thanks — I’ll follow up with karthik for the technical note and monica for SOW details.

Best,
Neha Kapoor
Account Executive, Redwood Inference
neha_kapoor@redwood.com | +1 (415) 555-0123

Subject: Re: Post-demo recap + data handling asks (BrightPath)

Neha — thanks for the clear recap. A couple of clarifying Qs from our side before we pick A/B/C: 

• By “0-retention” do you mean absolutely no persistent writes of request/response content to any durable store, or that logs are kept only in-memory and flushed on instance termination? We need explicit wording for contracts.
• What telemetry will you still retain (IP, timestamp, model/route identifiers, usage counters)? Our security team will need to know what can be sampled/aggregated.
• For option B (Private), what is the typical lead time and estimated incremental cost versus Hosted?

Procurement (procurement@brightpath.ai) is on copy — they’ll handle SOW redlines once we internalize the technical constraints. Also, SOC 2 evidence will be necessary for our audit team — can you indicate where in your stack audit logs are retained and how we can get a read-only extract if required?

Appreciate the quick follow-up.

—Elaine
Director of Product, BrightPath Analytics
elaine.chu@brightpath.ai
From: Karthik Iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.com>
To: Elaine Chu <elaine.chu@brightpath.ai>, Tim Lee <timothy.lee@brightpath.ai>
Cc: Neha Kapoor <neha_kapoor@redwood.com>, Monica Patel <monica_patel@redwood.com>
Date: Mon, 28 Sep 2026 11:24:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Post-demo recap + data handling asks (BrightPath)

Elaine / Tim — Karthik from Redwood security/infra here. Answering the technical points and proposing concrete contract language you can evaluate. 

1) Definition of 0-retention (hosted): 
   - For our hosted API, 0-retention means request/response payloads that include PII are not written to any persistent backing store by default. Processing occurs in-memory and ephemeral KV pages for the model runtime; these are not checkpointed to durable storage.
   - Short-lived traces (in-memory) may exist during the request lifecycle and are evicted immediately after processing. These traces are not searchable or accessible via our console.

2) Telemetry we retain (always): 
   - Aggregated usage metrics (per-customer token counts, aggregate latency percentiles).
   - Route/model identifiers and non-PII derived metrics (no PII content in telemetry).
   - Audit metadata: timestamps and a hashed request identifier (one-way) used only for incident correlation.

3) SOC 2 / audit logs: 
   - We can provide our SOC 2 Type II report and a read-only extract of platform audit logs scoped to administrative actions. Platform request logs (payloads) are not included when 0-retention is in effect.

4) Proposed contract language (short): 
   - “Redwood will not persist customer request/response content containing PII in hosted environments when Customer elects 0-retention processing for specified API routes.”
   - “Redwood will retain operational telemetry as described in Appendix A (aggregated metrics and hashed correlation ids) for security and billing purposes.”

5) Practical considerations & alternatives:
   - Debugging: a true 0-retention posture makes in-flight debugging harder. We recommend a short debug-window (default 7 days) that can be disabled per-route; all access to debug traces requires documented approvals and is audited.
   - Private/Dedicated: If BrightPath requires an absolute contractual guarantee of zero-persist for all artifacts (including transient diagnostics), our private deployment option (VPC or on-prem) is recommended — this provides tenant-controlled logging and optional HSM/KMS integration.

Attachments: I’m attaching a one-page DPIA note and suggested SOW paragraph for retention carveouts.

If that helps, we can mark the SOW to include an operational rollback policy and a canary period for any retention relaxations. Happy to jump on a 30-min sync with your security/procurement this week — suggest Thu 10/1 at 11:00am PT.

—Karthik Iyer
Security & Compliance, Redwood Inference
karthik_iyer@redwood.com

Attachments: BrightPath_DPIA_v1.pdf (same draft), Retention_Carveout_SOW_paragraph.docx

Subject: Re: Post-demo recap + data handling asks (BrightPath)

Thanks Karthik — that level of detail is helpful. BrightPath is comfortable with the hosted 0-retention definition you provided as long as two things are true: 

1) Aggregate telemetry remains non-PII and is defined in the appendix (we’ll review Appendix A).
2) You include a clause that for debugging Redwood will require formal sign-off and that debug traces will be retained only for the explicitly-approved window.

Procurement is looping in to take the SOW through redlines (procurement@brightpath.ai). We’ll aim to get redlines back by next Wed. Our security team will also want to review the SOC 2 artifact and the DPIA. Please send the SOC 2 package and the DPIA final draft.

We’re aligned on the canary + rollback approach. Confirm the 10/1 sync if you’re available and we’ll send calendar.

—Tim
